body.statement: For each fixed \(t\) and cell \(x\), the sharp extrema of \(\nu_x(D(0)>t,R(1)\le r)\) are \(A^L_x(r,t)\) and \(A^U_x(r,t)\). One coupling attains \(A^U_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\), and another coupling attains \(A^L_x(r,t)\) simultaneously for every \(r\le t\). Therefore the standardized coordinate bounds follow by summing with weights \(p_x/S(t)\), and the sharp RM-SACE interval is obtained by integrating the opposite common TV-SACE envelopes along that fixed cohort.
body.justification: Coordinatewise sharpness does not justify integration; common extremizers are the missing mathematical reason that fixed-cohort RM-SACE envelope integration is exact.
body.gap: Chen, Cui, and Yang integrate threshold bounds for a scalar survivor outcome, while the opened papers do not prove one coupling jointly attains all readmission thresholds for a nested survivor cohort.
body.consumer: It gives a closed-form RM-SACE sensitivity region without solving a new optimization problem at every integration point.
